notes: One optimized executable and workspace feature graph for every variant.
Fixed batch width 16; rows=1000 matches the production adaptive maximum for 1/8 workers.
Synthetic inline 128-byte state; construct futures, spawn, poll, send completions and drain inside timing. No Bowl, planning, fetch guards, memo or commit.
Typed: concrete rows/tasks. Boxed: one BoxFuture per row. Shared task: concrete rows with one erased outer task future.
Return count/checksum assertions run outside timing. Results pass black_box after timing.
Active workstation; two fresh processes per variant in rotating/reversed order. No speed acceptance threshold.

method_notes: CPU profiles use cpu-clock:u at 499 Hz with DWARF stacks; only the spawned fixture process and inherited threads are sampled.
FIFO enable/disable acknowledgements bound the request lifecycle. Setup, warmup, statistics reads, assertions, formatting and final world destruction are excluded.
Unsampled rounds are separate from perf rounds. CPU shares are fractions of sampled process user CPU, not fractions of wall time.
Per-system poll counters sum elapsed poll durations across workers and include fetch/guard/output costs; they are not pure kernel CPU time.
Plan time, settle time and snapshot time overlap; the existing commit bucket covers hook commits only and cannot measure streamed publication.
Leaf groups are exclusive name-based lower-bound categories, not exhaustive engine-stage attribution. Full leaf/caller tables and per-round sampled counters remain in target/execution-profile.
One-worker isolated results are variable and include regressions. The eight-worker tiny typed/boxed separation repeats, while task-only erasure remains close.
No inferred whole-engine speedup or Amdahl ceiling is calculated from CPU shares; paths overlap in time.
